[[Category:Utilities]]
=Gibbed's Dwarf Fortress Tileset Compiler=

[[Image:Dwarf Fortress Tileset Compiler Example Zoomed.png|right|example of a created tileset]]
Tileset Compiler (or ''TSC'' for short) is a utility for Dwarf Fortress created by [[User:Rick|Rick]] which attempts to ease the creation of graphical creature tilesets.

It is written in C# and requires the [http://www.microsoft.com/downloads/details.aspx?FamilyID=0856eacb-4362-4b0d-8edd-aab15c5e04f5 .NET 2.0 Runtime].

==Features==

*Tileset images will be created properly aligned in width and height so that Dwarf Fortress will load them correctly - this means images that are not a multiple of 4 will function correctly (15x15 tilesets!).

*A checkboard pattern will be drawn so it is easier to distinguish tiles.

*Ensures that tiles do not overlap same positions, and will warn about such.

*Tiles will be centered horizontally if too small width wise, and aligned to the bottom if too small height wise.

==Usage==

TSC is currently a console-based utility. Future versions may sport a proper UI.

To use TSC, all you have to do is specify a '''graphics_name.txt''' file for it to parse and build a tileset from.

It will attempt to open images based on definitions found in the file - it will attempt to first open a PNG, then a TGA, then a BMP.

All paths loaded and saved to are relative to the input file name given to TSC.

===Example===

====Input====

<tt>tsc.exe graphics_example.txt</tt>

====Output====

<tt>Warning: Could not find tiles\dwarves\default\dwarf_default_default<br />
Warning: Could not find tiles\dwarves\default\dwarf_default_miner<br />
Created C:\DF\tscexample\example/dwarves.bmp</tt>

====Explanation====

TSC loads graphics_example.txt, sees two entries, <tt>[DEFAULT:DWARVES:0:0:ADD_COLOR]</tt> and <tt>[MINER:DWARVES:1:0:AS_IS:DEFAULT]</tt>.

It derives the following file names from these entries:
*<tt>tiles\dwarves\default\dwarf_default_default</tt>
*<tt>tiles\dwarves\default\dwarf_default_miner</tt>

This is from the following format:

<tt>tiles\''tile page name''\''state name''\''tile page name''_''state name''_''profession name''</tt>

When loading an image:

*It checks for it in three different formats: PNG, TGA, and BMP.

*If it finds one it will load and use it.

*If it does not find one, and it is a <tt>CHILD</tt> profession, it will check for a <tt>DEFAULT</tt> image and will load and use it.

*If it still does not, then it will check for <tt>tiles\missing.png</tt> and load and use it.

*If that still does not, it will not draw any tile at all.
